comparison: Strong agreement on claims C89-C94 regarding chemotaxis and endosomal signaling. Both evaluations find the transwell migration data in Figure 7 convincing. OpenEval notes the experiments are in a single cell line, while peer reviewers accept the findings without challenge.

Strong agreement on claims C80-C88 regarding Rac1 activation from endosomes. Both evaluations support the comprehensive NanoBiT data with pharmacological and genetic interventions. Peer reviewers note this builds on earlier Legler group findings, while OpenEval emphasizes the convergent evidence from multiple inhibitors.

Strong agreement on claims C25-C32 regarding differential effects of CCL19 vs CCL21 on β-arrestin recruitment and internalization. Both evaluations accept the Figure 1 characterization data. OpenEval emphasizes the complementary assays and statistical analysis, while peer reviewers note these verify previous studies and are foundational.

Agreement on claims C33-C35 regarding cAMP signaling. Both evaluations accept the data showing equivalent inhibition by both ligands. Peer review R6 groups these with the broader Figure 1 characterization, while OpenEval separately evaluates the sustained signaling aspect.

Strong agreement on claims C52-C60 regarding spatial resolution of G protein activation at endosomes. Both evaluations support the EbBRET and microscopy data in Figure 3. Peer reviewers emphasize this verifies endomembrane signaling from previous studies, while OpenEval notes functional consequences require further investigation.

Agreement on claims C48-C51 regarding endosomal Gi/o activation. Both evaluations accept the NanoBiT biosensor data with PTX controls. Peer review R2 groups these with broader endosomal G protein signaling claims (C52-C60), while OpenEval evaluates the Rap1GAP biosensor data separately.

Agreement on claims C36-C40 regarding β-arrestin tail conformation. Both evaluations support the EbBRET data with β-arrestin1-ΔFL mutant. Peer review R1 groups these with megaplex formation claims (C41-C47), while OpenEval evaluates them separately, emphasizing differential CCL19 vs CCL21 effects.

Agreement on claims C41-C47 regarding megaplex formation. Both evaluations support the NanoBiT and confocal microscopy data. Peer reviewers state experiments are 'well controlled and executed,' while OpenEval emphasizes the complementary approaches and visual evidence for co-localization at endosomes.

Strong agreement on claims C61-C70 regarding APEX2 proteomics identifying CCR7 microenvironment proteins. Both evaluations emphasize the value of this resource. Peer reviewers call it 'the most novel findings' and 'valuable to the GPCR and immunology community,' while OpenEval notes appropriate controls but highlights that functional significance requires validation.

Agreement on claims C71-C75 regarding EYA2 and novel partners identified by APEX2. Both evaluations support these findings as part of the proteomics resource. Peer review R3 groups these with the broader APEX2 dataset, while OpenEval separately notes that functional roles remain to be validated.

Agreement on claims C76-C77 regarding differential enrichment of regulators in different compartments. Both evaluations accept these APEX2 findings. Peer review R3 includes these in the overall proteomics resource evaluation, while OpenEval notes functional validation is needed.

Agreement on claims C78-C79 regarding spatial localization and pathway activation. Both evaluations support the NanoBiT data. OpenEval notes the interpretation that spatial localization does not matter is reasonable but could benefit from more direct experiments, while peer reviewers accept the findings without this caveat.

Agreement on claims C1-C24 representing established knowledge and context. Both evaluations accept these background claims and citations. Peer reviewers note the 'excellent narrative,' while OpenEval emphasizes these provide necessary context but are not novel findings. Both accept the C-terminal tail sequence analysis in Table 1.

Agreement on claims C95-C114 representing literature citations supporting interpretation. Both evaluations accept these references as appropriate context. Peer review R7 implicitly accepts the contextual framework through noting the narrative quality, while OpenEval explicitly states these are appropriately referenced and provide important context for receptor internalization and Rac1 signaling.
